thread:
anya: follow-up to the onboarding pipeline thread  quick sync on a lightweight validator-handshake pattern that can survive noisy models and partial golden availability. want to lock the minimum contract so runners + validators can be developed in parallel.

anya: doc snippet: https://go.internal/prod/design/validator-handshake-compact (please comment inline)

marco: high-level ok. i'm strongly in favour of ~explicit demotion instead of infinite retries. otherwise a bad model will sit in the queue and starve others.

liam: agree. suggest a capped retry window + per-model token-rate budget. e.g. allow up to 10 attempts over 5 minutes OR until token_budget used. That prevents long-tail retries.

priya: can we define the states simply so operators can reason about them? my vote: NEW -> SENT -> RETRYING -> DEFERRED -> ESCALATED. ESCALATED means human review.

ops-bot: FYI: our current tools only index up to 100k deferred items per project. we should avoid bulk deferrals for models with micro-bursts.

anya: good call. config idea (compact):

```yaml
handshake_v1:
  max_attempts: 6
  retry_policy: exponential_jitter
  min_backoff_ms: 150
  max_backoff_ms: 8000
  demote_threshold_secs: 90  # if repeated failures within this window -> DEFERRED
  deferred_ttl_hours: 24
  per_model_budget:
    checks_per_minute: 5
    tokens_per_hour: 25000
```

tess: minor tweak  calls out that "per_model_budget" should be soft (throttle) not hard (reject) for hosted so we can still admit emergency canaries. soft throttle should surface in telemetry.

marco: golden rotation: we must be conservative. proposal: only update golden set during a promoted model rollout step (manual or CI-approved). For nightly auto-rotations we can create a shadow golden that doesn't affect primary regressions.

liam: also add a compact fallback artifact ("mini-golden") that's 10-20 deterministic prompts for quick unblock. If the validator reports missing golden, runner uses mini-golden and flags for ops.

priya: telemetry minimum (compact list): request_id, model_sha, handshake_version, state, attempts, elapsed_ms, golden_status (ok|missing|corrupt|mismatch), seqlen_p50/p95, kv_cache_mb, node_id. Trace sampling: 0.5% general, 100% for ADMIT/CANARY.

anya: also include an optional field "golden_hint" where validator can provide accepted_golden_id to help operator triage. keep it short.

ops-bot: note: previous incidents show golden_hash alone isn't enough when tokenizers differ. suggest tagging tokenizer_version in handshake.

marco: agreed. add tokenizer_version + runtime_build_id. Also let's version the handshake schema (v1) so older runners degrade gracefully and validator returns "schema_unsupported" with a recommended upgrade URL.

tess: CLI requests from ops: swap-golden, requeue-deferred <filter>, inspect-deferred <model>. can we make that part of repo ops-tooling? avoids ad-hoc scripts.

anya: tradeoff section: single-binary vs split-service: single-binary reduces network complexity and simplifies file-access for on-prem installs; split-service scales validator independently and isolates load. Recommendation: support both modes via feature flag and clear deploy docs.

liam: one more thought: expose a short-lived diagnostic token in the handshake that allows the validator to fetch extra debug traces from runner if the validation run fails silently. TTL 10m. Helps postmortem without over-indexing logs.

priya: actionable next steps:
- anya: land a minimal handshake schema + examples (today)
- tess: inventory telemetry + add tokenizer/runtime fields (tomorrow)
- marco: add per-model soft-budget knobs to the config draft (EOD)
- liam: prototype mini-golden artifact and a CLI command to swap (next week)

anya: if no objections i'll open a tiny RFC follow-up PR that contains the schema (compact json) and a short compatibility note for old runners. :thumbsup: 

marco: +1

liam: +1 :rocket:
